column6: Evidence ladder note: zero Apple sample code — shipped repo source outranks docs and talks throughout this part
GRAPH and EAGER are separate implementations with different configs and bugs — not guaranteed to produce equivalent models
enable_per_channel_scale=True lowers to rank-6 LUTs the ANE (max rank 5) rejects — the model silently moves to GPU
Compute-unit fallback is documented and silent — correct outputs, several times slower, visible only in tooling
Evidence note: no Apple sample code — quantization claims rest on coreai-opt source and shipped recipes
A block size the weight isn't divisible by yields only a warning and an uncompressed layer
Table of contents pointer to the consolidated silent-failures section
The session transcript's claim about EAGER mode does not match the shipped behavior — a discrepancy worth knowing
A field set to None is not the same as omitting it — the two spell different quantization configs
module_type_configs keyed by the string 'torch.nn.Linear' silently matches nothing — use the class object
The 'dynamic' range calculator cannot be exported — finalize() raises NotImplementedError naming each affected module
A block size your weight isn't divisible by leaves the layer uncompressed, with only a log line
Block-size mismatch is caught internally and swallowed — the fake-quantize disables itself and the layer ships uncompressed
Graph and eager modes do not produce equivalent quantized models — switching modes changes numerics
Now-fixed axis bug in coreai::quantize/dequantize — worth knowing when reading older artifacts
axis=-1 normalized off by one — per-channel scales landed one dim early with no shape error when sizes match (fixed #24)
Annotation limits: chains longer than 2 raise, and sequential matching requires each op type in the chain to be unique
Graph mode overrides six ops' qschemes for backend correctness — eager mode performs none of these adjustments
Pool/flatten share one FakeQuantize between input and output — a per-channel scale can land on the wrong axis
Archive holds opposite int8 orderings for different tensor roles — int8 is the safe floor; which int8 is empirical
Open bug follows: shared weights blend two configs — dtype from one, QAT schedule from the other
A shared weight takes dtype from one config and fake-quant schedule from another — issue #41, open, no warning
KV-cache quant ops must commute with quantize/dequantize — point it at arithmetic and the export succeeds, wrongly
Talk says 4-bit on the two encoders; the shipped recipe is asymmetric — image w4/gs32, text w6/gs8
Talk says per-channel scales; the shipping recipe sets enable_per_channel_scale=False and uses grouped-channel granularity
--n-bits and --group-size override BOTH encoders — passing 4 silently drags the text encoder down from w6/gs8
Return value vs in-place mutation: Apple's own docs give both readings of the casting passes
One doc says the casting passes mutate in place and return nothing; the signatures return ExportedProgram — a conflict
The casting pass changes user input/output dtypes in place — feeding fp32 afterwards presents as garbage, not a type error
fp16 casting does not guard activation overflow, and compression makes previously-safe values overflow
fp16-cast models can emit zeros where stable ops yield large finite values — activation overflow is unguarded (#7, open)
palettize_weights' lut_dtype is positional #2 with no default — docs pass it as a keyword, hiding the trap; XOR rules apply
Consolidated index of this guide's quantization silent failures
Diffusion path swallows quantization failures with a warning — you can ship a full-precision model believing it compressed
ChannelStructured(axis=-1) prunes the wrong channels — per-channel L1 norms collapse to a scalar (PR #45 open)
aten.cat on packed intx/uintx tensors drops dim — every cat runs on dim 0, (2,4)+(2,4) dim=1 gives (4,4) (PR #41 open)
The talk's third row has no number — 'a fraction of the size' is unquantified; don't invent one
Per-channel axis-0 int8 Linear weights return garbage on the macOS-27-beta GPU delegate — use per-block-32 there
Evidence note: no Apple sample code — palettization claims rest on coreai-opt source and Apple's shipped recipes
Covered here: the ANE rank-5 ceiling — one palettization flag silently reroutes the model to the GPU
Contents pointer: the ANE rank-5 ceiling section
Contents pointer: consolidated silent failures
group_size=1 means one LUT per output channel — the LUT overhead is why Apple's presets use 8/16/32
PerTensorGranularity exists twice with the same spelling in different modules — importing the wrong one misconfigures
shape[axis] % group_size must be 0 — a non-dividing group size leaves the layer unpalettized with only a warning
The ANE rank-5 ceiling: rank-6 tensors force the op — and its fused neighbors — off the Neural Engine
enable_per_channel_scale improves PyTorch numerics slightly and silently moves the model to GPU — invisible on a Mac
export.py --n-bits applies to both encoders — 4 silently drags the text encoder from its 6-bit/gs8 default
Scalar palettization is reproducible; vector palettization is not — identical builds differ
A vector-palettized model differs every rebuild of the identical commit — golden-hash regression tests fail mysteriously
Eager-only KMeansPalettizer.finalize() frees the dense float weights — there is no undo
finalize() discards float weights with no warning — if prepare() mutated your only copy, the float model is gone
Realized sparsity rounds down — an unreachable channel target can round to zero pruning
floor(8 channels x 0.1) = 0: the layer is untouched, no warning — your '10% sparse' model is 0% sparse in narrow layers
lut_dtype is positional #2 with no default — pass positionally and your n_bits lands in the lut_dtype slot
Registry preset YAMLs exist only in the source tree — wheel installs SystemExit; clone coreai-models to read the recipes
The 76% figure needs backbone-feature caching CoreAISegmentationEngine doesn't do — it re-runs image_encode every call
Beta-era measurement with an identified but unconfirmed mechanism — record toolchain versions with every sweep result
Two opposite int4/int8 findings measured at different dates on different roles — do not flatten them into one rule
Author's caveats: quick-driver tok/s ~10x too slow, only the ratio is valid; flagship int4 has a known quality cost
The one-flag experiment is one author's result on one model family — verify on your own model before adopting
uv run implicitly syncs and can clobber group-pinned venv packages — Apple's own AGENTS.md says always pass --no-sync
128 eval samples: a 1.5-point difference is inside noise — trust the ordering, not the magnitudes
Consolidated index of palettization/pruning silent failures
prepare() succeeds while mis-sized layers were never compressed — the model ships bigger than your release notes say
'torch.nn.Linear' has dots so it passes the syntactic check and then matches nothing — genuinely silent
ResNet50 PTQ numbers rest on 128 eval samples (896 calibration) — indicative, not conclusive
The 76%-faster second inference requires caller-side caching Apple's package does not do
Community table is a single-author archive with self-declared uncontrolled benchmarks — not Apple figures
2.18x dense-int4km ratio: author says absolute tok/s are ~10x too slow — only the ratio is valid
Import the palettization PerTensorGranularity — not the identically-named quantization one
Cheat sheet: enable_per_channel_scale=True means rank-6 LUT, ANE rejection, and silent GPU fallback
Evidence note: no Apple sample code — the format matrix rests on SDK headers, shipped source, and doc prose
A format the compute unit lacks doesn't throw — specialization silently reassigns the op several-times-slower elsewhere

Matrix legend: warning-marked cells are supported only with the caveat named in the referenced section
fp32 matmuls on MLX's NAX path silently run at TF32 relaxed precision unless MLX_ENABLE_TF32 disables it
int16 sits in the TensorOps enum but the Metal-language type map has no int16 mapping — the int16 oddity
uint8 on the ANE is uncertain — Apple's rule file names only fp16/int8/int16 as ANE compute dtypes
int4 is storage, not compute — the int4b_format Metal type is gated behind a feature macro
uint4 mirrors int4: storage-only, with the same Metal feature-macro gate
MXFP4 emit is validator-enforced: per-block-32 with E8M0 scales, or ValueError — nothing else counts as MXFP4
k-means palettes: eager-mode only, with a caveat on the recipe path (§2.5) — indices store as sub-byte ints
Complex dtypes exist in MLX but are excluded from NAX — complex matmuls run on the older, slower kernels
A block size the weight doesn't divide by leaves the layer at full precision — a warning is the only trace
The fake-quantize logs 'Skipping quantization' and permanently disables itself — graph mode then removes the node
The casting passes mutate the program and change user I/O dtypes — old callers feed fp32 and get garbage, not an error
Framework page lists seven platforms; every symbol page's platform array omits macOS and Catalyst — a docs-generation bug
Sub-byte nibble order is undocumented — the decode assumes MLX's low-first convention; verify on a known tensor first
64-bit types are narrowed on the way in: int64 to int32 and fp64 to fp32, silently
The converter narrows int64/fp64 to 32-bit silently — NDArray has 64-bit ScalarTypes the converter never produces
A bare Python float literal can move an op — and its fused pattern — off the ANE to the GPU
A literal fp16 can't represent materializes as an fp32 constant — the consuming op leaves the ANE with no warning
Apple accepted a known quality regression to avoid a silent compute-unit fallback — the ranking this guide argues for
Session 325 narration says per-channel scales; shipped code sets enable_per_channel_scale=False — both readings are live
Recognized entrypoint names select the sample loader's ANE preference — rename them and you get the GPU policy
CoreAISegmentationEngine re-runs image_encode on every call and exposes no cache — the headline speedup needs your code
Two different version numbers are both correct — they answer different questions; report both, not one
Undefined __HAVE_TENSOR__ empties the whole header — the only symptom is a distant 'no member named matmul2d'
OS 27 multi-plane tensors: compute/render usage only, one-byte data elements, no rank-0 — keep a software fallback
No API reports NAX support — MLX infers it from GPU architecture generation; there is no supportsFamily query
MLX's own caveat: mxfp8 results differ on <1% of elements and can exceed 1 ULP for small values; nvfp4 matches exactly
MLX ships its own FP4/FP8 bit-manipulation structs — distinct from Xcode 27's Metal tensor datatypes
A deployment target below 26.2 silently drops every NAX kernel — the only trace is a CMake configure-time warning
MLX float32 matmuls silently run at TF32 on the NAX path — PR #3883 exists because users keep being surprised
NAX changes which algorithm is selected (its own split-K), not just which kernel — it is not a drop-in accelerator
--quant-predicate works only with --q-mode affine and needs down_proj modules — otherwise a ValueError
Failure #1: non-dividing block_size leaves the layer uncompressed; only one logger.warning marks it
Failure #2: per-channel-scale palettes lower to rank-6 LUTs — the whole op silently moves to GPU
Failure #3: an fp32 operand makes the node fp32 and ANE-ineligible — check Compute types in the model viewer
Failure #4: an epsilon fp16 can't represent (1e-6) fails the round-trip predicate — same silent ANE exit
Failure #5: F.silu lowers to cast+swish(f32)+cast — three ANE-invalid ops from one call
Failure #6: one dynamic dimension breaks the ANE's fully-static-shape requirement — silently ineligible
Failure #7: FP8/FP4 weights have no ANE compute path — execution lands on GPU or CPU
Failure #8 is by design: int4 is storage — the runtime dequantizes to fp16/half for arithmetic; nothing to fix
Failure #11: MLX built below target 26.2 drops all NAX kernels — semi-silent, one configure-time warning
Failure #12: MLX fp32 matmul at default env runs TF32 relaxed precision — set MLX_ENABLE_TF32=0 and diff
Failure #13: an MLX layer whose last dim doesn't divide group_size is silently skipped by the quant predicate
Failure #15: int64 index tensors are narrowed to int32 — values above INT32_MAX overflow, mostly unclamped
Failure #16: IEEE -inf softmax masks compute wrong numbers on the ANE — use -40000.0 instead
Failure #17: diffusion components that fail quantization are swallowed with a warning — check file size on disk
Failure #18: coreai_kit.run defaults to cpu_only — benchmarks copying those defaults silently measure the CPU
Diffusion quantization failures are swallowed (export/compiler.py) — cross-check on-disk size against numel x bits/8
The one-line check: if you targeted the ANE, confirm the viewer's Compute types show no float32
The Xcode model viewer itself requires the Metal Toolchain, which is not installed by default
Summary asymmetry: storageTypes and operationDistribution carry counts; the compute-side listing does not
includingStatistics:true is considerably slower on large models — false returns versions and signatures, enough to probe
The debug gauge needs a direct CoreAI.framework link — reach Core AI through a package and the gauge never appears
AOT compiles only for Apple-Intelligence hardware: A17 Pro+, M1+ Macs, M2+ Vision Pro — one .aimodelc per arch
Consolidated index of format-related silent failures
The M5 talk's baselines differ per claim — M4 for images, M1 for video; cite the baseline with the number
ResNet50 PTQ row: int8 and FP8-E4M3 land within ~2.4 points of fp32 — the most directly useful format-choice datum
Beta bug, not a fallback: per-channel axis-0 int8 Linear weights return wrong numbers on the macOS-27-beta GPU delegate
Methodology: curl via sosumi.ai preserves verbatim signatures the rendered docs sometimes reflow
111432 is a Tech Talk, not a WWDC session — cite it accordingly
